finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts::new pptx export path fetches arbitrary, collaborator-controlled image `src` values with `credentials: "include"` and no host allowlist (client-side ssrf / credentialed request forgery)
evidence: Verified export-utils.ts:41-51 (`fetch(resolved, { credentials: "include" })`) and resolveImageUrl's deliberate pass-through of any absolute scheme, plus pptx-actions.ts's `fetchImage: docsImageFetcher` and pptx/index.ts step 2 / `extFromMime` (no size cap, unknown MIME defaults to .png), and docs-content.controller.ts `assertValidElement`, which validates only id/type/frame — so collaborator-controlled `data.src` really does reach a credentialed fetch with no host allowlist, and the pptx-actions docstring's "same-origin-fetched" claim is not enforced. Impact is far smaller than the claim implies, though: `credentials: "include"` sends the target origin's own cookies (not the victim's Wafflebase session), the default cors mode makes non-CORS cross-origin responses unreadable so the export just fails, and the editor already emits requests to the same srcs via plain `img.src` when the deck is viewed — so the delta is request emission (beacon / unauthenticated intranet GET), not exfiltration. Rated minor: a genuine missing-allowlist hygiene defect on an additional call site, not a critical SSRF.
